# Ahmet Kazankaya

> AI automation engineer based in Istanbul, Turkey. Builds the platform layer that makes LLM agents safe to run in production: execution runtimes, human approval gates, permission boundaries, run logging and evaluation harnesses. Ships native macOS, iOS, Windows and web tools as a solo builder. Open to full-time roles in Europe, on site or remote.

Ahmet Kazankaya works as a solo product builder: product and interface design, implementation and testing, with coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) as part of the process. A task management system built for Türkiye Maarif Vakfı, a foundation operating schools in 66 countries, has been in production for four months. Other running work includes an Etsy and Printify automation line with a Telegram approval gate, an ESP32-S3 desk robot with a speech pipeline, and open source Claude Code skill sets that other people install.

Skills: LLM agent orchestration, workflow automation, evaluation harnesses, CI reliability gates, prompt engineering, retrieval augmented generation, Python, TypeScript, Swift and SwiftUI, FastAPI, Next.js, Docker, AWS, ESP32 firmware. Languages: Turkish, English.

Contact: ahmetkazankaya1@gmail.com, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ahmetkazankaya), [GitHub](https://github.com/kasparovabi).

- [Gecit privacy policy](https://kasparovabi.github.io/gecit/privacy.html)

## Open source

- [Sift](https://github.com/kasparovabi/sift): native macOS app that indexes local Claude Code and Codex session transcripts for full text search
- [DSH Studio](https://github.com/kasparovabi/dsh-studio): unofficial native macOS client for dsh, the DeepSeek agent harness
- [Cutaway](https://github.com/kasparovabi/cutaway): native macOS app that transcribes a video and matches short clips to every sentence
- [Busted](https://github.com/kasparovabi/busted): a Mac desk guard that catches snoops
- [claude-audit-20](https://github.com/kasparovabi/claude-audit-20): guard-20 and audit-20 for Claude Code, twenty AI coding failure classes as write time rules plus a twenty pass verification gate with a false positive filter
- [motion-first-design](https://github.com/kasparovabi/motion-first-design): Claude Code skill for motion first web design, published with the blind ablation that proved its first version wrong
- [claude-file-bridge](https://github.com/kasparovabi/claude-file-bridge): uploads real files to a page when browser automation file upload is broken
- [embeddinggemma2-rag-test](https://github.com/kasparovabi/embeddinggemma2-rag-test): EmbeddingGemma 2 GGUF settings for RAG compared against each other and BM25
- [strands-decider-eval](https://github.com/kasparovabi/strands-decider-eval): AWS Strands Decider 2B tested on 501 real CI failures and 500 Wordle games
- [iMenu timing fix](https://github.com/meyusufdemirci/iMenu-MacOS/pull/1): event ordering fix merged upstream into a macOS menu bar manager
- [claude-mythos-scaffold](https://github.com/kasparovabi/claude-mythos-scaffold): retired August 2026, agent persistence scaffold for older Claude models

### Template Studio

Category: Web. Turn everyday announcements into consistent, ready to export designs.

Problem: Routine institutional announcements share a visual system but carry different names, dates and contact details. Recreating each layout manually makes consistency harder to maintain.

My work: I designed and built the template collection, editing forms, live previews and image export, including the layout rules for each announcement type.

Implementation: Typed template data feeds React layouts. The editor measures the available space to scale its preview, while export uses the original canvas dimensions and embedded fonts.

Result: A user can choose a template, enter the announcement details and export a JPG. Seven template routes cover appointment, departure, HR information, condolences and celebrations.

Stack: TypeScript, React, Next.js, html-to-image

Role: Solo creator · Product, design and engineering. I designed and built this project independently, including its interface and implementation.

Verification: All seven English template routes were exercised in the original browser editor. Each Download JPG action produced a readable JPEG with nonzero dimensions, with no broken browser images or download failures. The recording shows the original selection, editing and preview workflow.

Case study: https://kasparovabi.github.io/projects/maarif-sablon.html

### DSH Studio

Category: Desktop. A workspace for working with coding agents.

Problem: Working with a coding agent involves more than sending a prompt. Sessions, streamed output, tool approvals and model settings need to stay understandable as work progresses.

My work: I designed and built the macOS application: the session browser, live conversation interface, controls and integration with the dsh server.

Implementation: SwiftUI presents sessions while JSON RPC and a WebSocket event stream connect the interface to the existing dsh harness. History recovery reads the local session log when the server cannot serve a damaged transcript.

Result: The application brings session navigation, streaming output, approvals and configuration into one native workspace. The original repository includes the demonstration shown here.

Stack: Swift, SwiftUI, JSON RPC, WebSocket

Role: Solo creator · Product, design and engineering. I designed and built this project independently, including its interface and implementation.

Verification: Original repository demo recording. The restored native application builds and connects to the local server. Agent execution was not retested in this review.

Case study: https://kasparovabi.github.io/projects/dsh-studio.html

Source: https://github.com/kasparovabi/dsh-studio

### Sift

Category: Developer tools. Find and revisit coding conversations across projects.

Problem: Useful decisions and solutions accumulate across Claude Code and Codex transcripts. Remembering a previous solution does not necessarily mean remembering which session contains it.

My work: I designed and built Sift, from transcript ingestion and local indexing to the search interface and the flow for returning to a session.

Implementation: Provider specific readers normalize local transcripts into a SQLite index. FTS5 provides full text search with ranked results. The interface can open the original session in the appropriate agent.

Result: Search, filters and readable session details provide a route back to earlier work. The demonstration uses example transcripts with the real indexing and reading flow.

Stack: Swift, SwiftUI, SQLite, FTS5

Role: Solo creator · Product, design and engineering. I designed and built this project independently, including its interface and implementation.

Verification: Existing English browser version; 18 synthetic sessions indexed, pagination search and session reading verified in browser; 31 tests passed and terminal POST returned 403. Native clients not exercised.

Case study: https://kasparovabi.github.io/projects/sift.html

Source: https://github.com/kasparovabi/sift
